newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's first mark bond performs well - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's first mark bond performs well - dealers.

text.p: Lebanon launched its first mark bond on Tuesday which was well-received and oversubscribed, dealers said.
"(The bond has gone) very, very well," a spokesman in Frankfurt for Commerzbank AG, joint lead managers with Societe Generale said.
The 250 million mark five-year issue, priced at 101.625, was one-and-a-half times oversubscribed, he added.
It was reoffered at 99.75 at a spread of 175 basis points over the underlying 8.0 percent January 2002 German unity bond (GUFA).
The reoffer yield was 6.56 percent, he said.
The 175 b.p. spread came at the lower end of the expected 165-195 b.p. range.
"There is big demand for the deal due to the fact that it is Lebanon and it has rarity value," the spokesman said, adding the size was also manageable.
"Investors are very happy to buy. It's a very good, fair pricing for Lebanon. I think the job Lebanon did in its presentation here and the marketing on our side helped very much."
The issue was the Lebanese government's first venture into the German debt market following previous dollar-denominated Eurobond issues totalling $900 million since September 1994.
The issue was seen as a success on the Beirut market. A Beirut bonds trader who asked not to be identified told Reuters it was aggressively priced and came out very well.
"People can buy deutschemarks at 4.0 percent and place them at 6.5 percent on this issue, so it's a pickup of 2.5 percent," the trader said. -- Andrew Tarnowski, Beirut editorial (9611) 345723 345740
